legalNotice: HANDLING NOTICE. This is a numbered Council copy, the property of the Office of Strategic Continuity, held under the authority of the Council Charter. It is issued to one named reader and may be read only by that reader, in a controlled space, in physical form. It may not be reproduced, transcribed, summarised, photographed, scanned or entered into any information system. Loss of positive control of this copy, however brief, is to be reported in person to the Office of Internal Assurance before the end of the duty period. Unauthorised disclosure breaches the undertaking signed on admission to the OSC and will be dealt with under the internal discipline provisions of the Charter, in addition to any other proceedings that may apply.

charter.title: Article I: Purpose
charter.text: Continuity is not survival. Continuity is purpose sustained beyond crisis. This infrastructure exists not to shelter us from the end, but to ensure the Republic emerges whole from whatever that end may be.

charter.title: Article II: Membership and Succession
charter.text: The Council shall consist of eleven members, drawn from those offices of government and industry upon which the continuity of the Republic depends: four of Cabinet rank, three who direct the agencies charged with the nation's intelligence and security, two of senior military command, and two from the industries that arm and supply its defense. A seat belongs to the office it represents and passes with that office. When a member departs, the seat stands vacant not for want of a person but for want of a briefing; the successor shall be admitted within thirty days, and the departing member's copy of every Council record shall be destroyed before the successor's copy is issued. No member shall hold two seats, and no seat shall be held in absence.

charter.title: Article III: Authority and Revision
charter.text: The Council is the sole authority of the Office of Strategic Continuity. It acts by a majority of its members present and voting, seven constituting a quorum. This Charter, the Facility Inventory, and every instrument the Council names as governing may be revised by a majority of the full Council and by no lesser body. Authority delegated by the Council is held in trust; it returns to the Council upon the Council's word, without notice and without cause shown.

charter.title: Article IV: Facilities and Custody
charter.text: The facilities of the Office are held in custody for the nation and are the property of no department. Each shall stand under the command of an officer answerable to the Council through the chain established by directive, and each shall keep in ordinary times the readiness it will require in extraordinary ones. No facility shall be surrendered, disclosed or abandoned except by resolution of the Council. The cover under which a facility stands is part of that facility and shall be kept with the same care.

charter.title: Article V: Personnel and Compartmentation
charter.text: Those who serve the Office serve within the tiers and compartments the Council establishes. Each shall know what the work before them requires, and no more; this is not distrust but design. Admission to a compartment is a grant of the Council and may be withdrawn as it was given. The Office shall account for every person in its service, wherever posted or however carried, and the obligations of that service do not lapse with posting, transfer or release.

charter.title: Article VI: Reconstitution
charter.text: Upon the Council's determination that the ordinary institutions of government cannot continue, the Office shall execute the plans of reconstitution it maintains, receive into its facilities those designated essential, and sustain the functions of government until they can be restored in their proper form. The Council shall then sit without adjournment. Its first duty is restoration and not rule, and it shall relinquish each function as the lawful institution able to bear it is restored. The determination itself rests with the Council alone.

charter.title: Article VII: Secrecy and Records
charter.text: The existence of the Office is the first of its secrets. Its governing records shall be kept on paper, in the number of copies the Council directs and in no other form, and each copy shall be accounted for until it is destroyed. No member, officer or employee shall disclose the Office, its facilities or its purpose to any person not admitted to it, under any compulsion. What is not written cannot be lost; what must be written shall be kept as though the Republic depended upon it, for it does.

divisions.name: Facilities Engineering
divisions.mandate: Engineering authority for all facilities and tunnels: structures, life support plant, seals, power distribution and reactor plant engineering. Issues work orders, segment engineering sheets and maintenance schedules.

divisions.name: Personnel & Vetting
divisions.mandate: Recruitment, investigation under the OSC supplement, tier assignment, postings, transfers and probation. Maintains strength accounting and the personnel number register.

divisions.name: Comptroller
divisions.mandate: Programme accounts, cover line-item reconciliation across the four appropriating departments, cost returns to the Council and payroll disbursement.

divisions.name: Communications Security
divisions.mandate: Operates the key distribution network, accredits MERIDIAN workstations, issues tokens and passphrases, and runs the MERIDIAN Service Desk.

divisions.name: Medical Services
divisions.mandate: Clinical services at all staffed facilities, medical readiness standards, pharmaceutical and blood product rotation, and the surgical capability of the network.

divisions.name: Logistics & Reserves
divisions.mandate: Strategic reserves (food, water, medical, energy, armaments), supply movements by tram, generator fuel and reactor operations. Publishes reserve positions and burn-down figures.

divisions.name: Cover Operations
divisions.mandate: Maintains the surface cover facilities and their staffing arrangements, the cover-identity catalogue and the prepared public statements for every facility type.

divisions.name: Security Forces Command
divisions.mandate: Command of security forces at all facilities: post orders, armament issue, access control, guard rotation for DELTA sites, and escort of visitors and consists.

divisions.name: Intelligence & Analysis
divisions.mandate: Operates the intelligence fusion floor at ALPHA-01 and regional analysis cells at BETA sites. Produces threat assessments and the daily continuity summary.

compartments.name: KESTREL
compartments.scope: Transit engineering: segment engineering sheets, tunnel environmental data, rolling stock technical records, possession planning and the commissioning file for each segment.

compartments.name: HOLLOW
compartments.scope: Personnel matters concerning detached and unposted personnel: status declarations, strength reconciliations, and the records of personnel carried without a posting.

compartments.name: SEXTANT
compartments.scope: Network geography beyond the holder's assigned site: facility locations, connections and regional network layouts not otherwise released to the holder's tier.

compartments.name: TALLOW
compartments.scope: Strategic reserves positions by site and reactor operations: plant status, refuelling schedules, fuel inventory and burn-down planning figures.

compartments.name: BRIAR
compartments.scope: Assurance contingencies: the contingency protocols held by the Office of Internal Assurance, inquiry files and their dispositions.

compartments.name: QUARRY
compartments.scope: Council and governance: Council minutes and resolutions, seat succession records and the Charter articles above UMBRA/OSC RESTRICTED.

compartments.name: LANTERN
compartments.scope: ALPHA-03 records and vaults: the Records Division stacks, accession registers, and the seed and biological sample collections. Granted to all Records Division personnel on posting.

glossary.def: The list, maintained by the facility security officer, of persons authorised unescorted entry to a controlled area. Reissued on the first working day of each month and on any change of more than five names.

The invented-for-purpose appropriation account string under which a line item is obligated. Format: agency prefix, four-digit account, three-digit sub-account. Account codes are not unique to the OSC and appear in the published accounts of the parent department.

A time-limited elevation of an individual to the access level of the next higher tier for the duration of a named duty. Issued by a facility commander, recorded in the audit trail, and lapsing without notice at the end of the duty period. An acting credential does not confer the briefings associated with the higher tier.

The individual named on a routing slip as responsible for preparing the response to a tasking by its suspense date. Where no action officer is named, the action falls to the originating division head.

Excused absence without charge to annual leave, granted at the discretion of the facility commander. Personnel on administrative leave remain subject to recall and may not leave the sustainment radius of their assigned facility.
A packaged fan, coil and filter assembly serving one ventilation zone. Each AHU is tagged with its zone number and filter cycle. Abbreviated AHU.

Command and control hub. Deep underground installation (800 to 2,400 ft) with full life support, independent power generation, rail terminal and government reconstitution capability. Five installations, ALPHA-01 to ALPHA-05.

The yearly security awareness module required of all tiers. Completion is recorded against the personnel number; non-completion by the suspense date suspends print release and removable media privileges.
A records-management instruction suspending scheduled destruction of a document or series pending review. Only the Records Division may place or lift an archive hold.
The distribution of programme cost across 127 separate budget line items in DOD, DOE, DHS and FEMA appropriations so that no single account discloses the programme.

The security office record of workstation activity: windows opened, searches made, documents printed, redactions examined. Retained for the life of the individual's access plus seven years. The audit trail may be read by its subject.

The photo-identification card issued with a personnel number and tier stripe. Worn above the waist and visible at all times below the surface cover facility. A badge is not an access credential on its own; entry also requires the smart token and passphrase.
A logged event in which a badge was presented at a reader for which it held no authorisation. Three exceptions in a thirty-day period are referred to the facility security officer.
One sleeping position with its allocated share of air, water, rations and sanitation. Capacity figures are expressed in berths.

Regional operations centre. Medium-depth installation (400 to 800 ft) for regional coordination and intelligence fusion, with tram connection to its local ALPHA facility and limited long-term sustainability. Twelve installations.
A length of running line, bounded by signals, that may be occupied by one consist at a time. Rail blocks are numbered by segment and chainage; tram blocks by network and link.
The state of a block as reported by train detection: CLEAR, OCCUPIED, or POSSESSED. A block under possession reports POSSESSED regardless of detection.

The formal, recorded act of informing an individual of the existence and scope of a compartment, followed by signature of the compartment non-disclosure statement. A briefing is specific to a compartment and, where stated, to a facility.
A striped paper sack for classified waste awaiting destruction. Burn bags are numbered, sealed when two-thirds full, and logged on collection.
The six-week menu cycle issued by Food Service at each staffed facility. Rotation is aligned network-wide so that ration drawdown is uniform across sites.

The tunnel length certified to the Council as operational: 847 miles. Certified mileage is the only tunnel figure used in Council reporting and Tier 1 summaries. It is not derived from, and is not reconciled with, engineering mileage.
An unannounced end-of-shift inspection of workspaces for unsecured classified material. Findings are recorded as security violations against the occupant of the desk.

A named body of information access to which requires a specific briefing in addition to tier. Compartments are designated by codeword. Holding a compartment does not confer knowledge of any other compartment, including its name.
A train as formed for a movement: the vehicles coupled together, their order and their load. A consist is identified by its consist ID for the duration of the movement.
The movement identifier displayed on the dispatcher board, in the form segment, direction and serial. A consist ID may be suppressed on the board by Transit Control on instruction.
The capability of an organisation to continue its essential functions under any circumstances. Used in OSC documents in its ordinary federal sense where cover documents require it. Abbreviated COOP.
Internal MERIDIAN mail carrying a marking. Controlled mail may be forwarded only to addressees eligible for its marking.
The serial number of a physical copy of a controlled document, shown as COPY nn OF nn. Copies are accountable by number.
The Core Council of eleven Tier 1 members holding UMBRA/OSC UNRESTRICTED access and full network awareness. Revision authority for controlled documents rests with a Council majority.

The authentic government function under whose name a facility's surface installation is registered, staffed and budgeted. A cover identity is real at the surface: the staff are employed, the work is done and the reports are filed.

The surface-level government facilities at every ALPHA and BETA site that require regular cleared personnel access and so account for the movement of people and materiel above the underground installation.
The periodic assessment of a cover identity's public-records posture, visible staffing and continued plausibility. Due at intervals not exceeding eighteen months.
The coloured sheet bearing the marking that is attached to the front of every classified document while it is outside a container.
The prepared public explanation for a facility, its traffic and its expenditure. Prepared cover stories exist for all facility types.
A citation of another document by document number. A cross-reference does not confer access to the document cited.

The recorded withdrawal of a compartment from an individual, with signature of the termination statement. Debriefing follows any facility transfer, separation, or change in duty that removes the need-to-know.

Safe house or equipment cache at surface or minimal depth, for emergency staging and equipment storage. Sustainability 72 hours maximum. No integrated transit connection. Twelve installations; detailed records Tier 1.
The range of depth below surface assigned to a facility class: ALPHA 800 to 2,400 ft; BETA 400 to 800 ft; GAMMA 150 to 500 ft; DELTA surface or minimal depth.
The form recording the destruction of a controlled document, signed by the destroying official and one witness, and filed with the Records Division.
Payroll category; see personnel accounting.
A numbered policy issuance with purpose, applicability, policy, responsibilities, procedures, references and supersession. Directives bind all tiers to which they are distributed.
The list of offices or copy numbers to which a document is issued. A document may not be passed to an office not on its distribution list without the originator's consent.
The two- to four-letter code identifying an originating division, used in document numbers, mail addresses and the originator field.
The unique identifier assigned to an OSC document under the canon numbering scheme. Document numbers are never reused, including after destruction.
A personal radiation dosimeter issued to personnel working in reactor spaces. Exchanged monthly; readings are recorded against the personnel number.
The officer holding authority for a facility outside normal hours. The duty officer's name is posted at the operations desk and in MERIDIAN at the start of each watch.
The published schedule of watches and duties for a facility, issued weekly.
The date from which a directive or instruction applies. Where none is stated, the date of signature.

The tunnel length measured by Transit engineering from segment and link survey: 6,074 miles of rail across six segments and 10,538 miles of tram across four regional networks. Used for maintenance, possession planning and the transit dispatcher board. Not used in Council reporting.
The signed transfer of accountable equipment to an individual. Equipment on issue is recorded against the personnel number and must be returned before any transfer.
A cleared individual accompanying a visitor or a person without unescorted access. The escort remains within sight of the escorted person at all times and is accountable for them.

Persons whose preservation is required for continuity of government and of the functions the network supports. Selection criteria are set by the Council and are not published below Tier 2. GAMMA-class shelters are intended for essential personnel only.
A point on a planned route for the movement of essential personnel to a sheltering facility. Certain DELTA-class sites are sited at extraction route nodes.
The Tier 2 officer in command of a facility, with full awareness of the assigned facility and its immediate connections.
A scheduled evacuation-to-refuge exercise. Below the surface cover facility, personnel evacuate to the nearest refuge chamber rather than to the surface.
The federal fiscal year, 1 October to 30 September, named for the calendar year in which it ends. Ledger figures are shown by fiscal year, FY2001 to FY2008.
The Phase 4 objective (2009 to 2012): network staffing at 40 per cent of capacity, 9,360 personnel. Abbreviated FOC.

One of the five appropriation streams from which programme cost is drawn: black budget intelligence programmes (41 per cent), DOD infrastructure (28), FEMA emergency preparedness (17), DOE site management (9), miscellaneous and reclassified (5).
Personnel shelter at shallow to medium depth (150 to 500 ft), for essential staff only. Basic life support; 90 to 180 day operational window. No rail connection. Eighteen installations.
The monthly loaded run of standby diesel generators. Diesel backup provides 180 days of runtime at all facilities.
The biological sample collection at ALPHA-03 (Level 9) holding genetic and biometric samples associated with essential personnel records. The holdings figure is controlled; see OSC-RSV-GENE.
The MERIDIAN display mode for small-screen field terminals: one window at a time, with an application switcher at the foot of the screen.
The scheduled interval between successive consists over the same block in the same direction. Minimum headway on rail segments is set by block length and braking distance at line speed.
A numbered request to Information Systems for workstation support. Tickets are visible to the requester, the help desk and the security office.

The scheduled replacement interval for particulate and gas-phase filters in each air handling unit. Standard cycle is 90 days for particulate pre-filters and 180 days for gas-phase beds; reactor spaces and seal-capable zones are on shortened cycles.
The form used to record a security, safety or equipment incident. Every incident report receives a number and an assigned action officer.
The individual responsible for issue, return and inventory of physical keys and combinations for a defined area.
The form by which annual or sick leave is requested. Leave for personnel within a probationary period is approved by the receiving division head, not the immediate supervisor.
One numbered floor of an underground facility, counted downward from Level 0, the surface cover facility. Level names above the holder's tier are withheld in facility documentation.
One of 127 budget lines in DOD, DOE, DHS and FEMA appropriations through which programme cost is carried. Each line item has a cover title, account code, funding source and programme category.
The status of a QKD circuit between two facilities as shown in the MERIDIAN notification area: UP, DEGRADED, or DOWN.

Loss of a badge is reported to the facility security officer within one hour of discovery. The badge is revoked, a temporary badge issued under escort, and an incident report raised. A second loss within twelve months is a security violation.
The modified magnetic levitation system used on the ALPHA-to-ALPHA rail network, operating at 180 mph average.

The classification designation applied to a document, banner or window: one of UMBRA/OSC EYES ONLY, UMBRA/OSC UNRESTRICTED, UMBRA/OSC COMPARTMENTED, UMBRA/OSC RESTRICTED, or TOP SECRET/SCI with OSC compartment.
The marking shown on the title area of each MERIDIAN window. The classification banner displays the highest marking among open windows.
The annual certification that an individual is fit for extended duty below ground and under seal. Lapsed medical readiness removes the individual from the seal roster.
The OSC closed internal network and its workstation environment, release 4.1.7. MERIDIAN has no external internet connectivity and carries traffic over the QKD network only.
The lowest staffing at which a facility can maintain its life support, power and security watches. Current skeleton crews are held at approximately a 7:1 ratio of support to command staff.
The isolation of a facility from outside air, water and access for nuclear, biological or chemical threat. All facilities are NBC-rated with 180-day seal capability.
The determination that an individual requires specific information to perform an assigned duty. Tier and compartment establish eligibility; need-to-know establishes access.
One of the four regional tram networks, Eastern, Southern, Mountain/Western and Central, each served by an ALPHA hub.
The body established in 2001 to construct and operate the facility network. Abbreviated OSC. The name does not appear in any published appropriation.
The workstation login identifier issued with a temporary access card or a permanent smart token.
The division and site that issued a document, shown as division code/facility.

The assignment of surface parking spaces at a cover facility. Allocation is set by the facility administrative officer so that vehicle counts at the surface are consistent with the cover identity's published staffing.
The memorised authenticator used with the operator ID and smart token. Passphrases are not written down outside the issuing envelope or temporary access card.
The monthly reconciliation of tier strength against posted facility strength, by payroll category. Categories other than POSTED are defined in the governing payroll issuance.
The unique number assigned to each individual on appointment, used in payroll, access control and the audit trail. Personnel numbers are never reissued.

One of five programme periods: Foundation (2001 to 2003), Infrastructure Build (2004 to 2006), Network Integration (2007 to 2008, active), Full Operational Capability (2009 to 2012) and Strategic Depth (2013 to 2020).

The exclusive occupation of a block or segment by engineering for maintenance, inspection or testing, during which no revenue movement is permitted. A possession is granted by Transit Control with stated limits and times.
The handling priority of a message: ROUTINE, PRIORITY, IMMEDIATE, or FLASH. Precedence governs delivery order, not importance.
A firm holding a direct construction or supply contract. Forty-seven primes, averaging 8.3 subcontractors each. No prime contractor is made aware of more than three facility sites.
The action of releasing a held print job at a secure printer by presenting the badge. Unreleased jobs are purged after four hours and logged.
Assignment to a new facility, which requires a new compartment briefing and a 90-day probationary period. During probation the individual may not hold an acting credential or approve their own leave.
A Defense budget classification number identifying a research, development or procurement programme, used as the cover title of some DOD line items.
Quantum-key distribution. The encrypted communications network carrying all OSC traffic, independent of standard government communications infrastructure.

The standard personnel distribution for a fully staffed ALPHA facility, based on the ALPHA-01 capacity of 4,500, across ten functions from Command and Administration (8 per cent) to Maintenance (5 per cent).
A scheduled test of a reactor protection or safety function, performed to a written procedure with results recorded in the reactor log. Eight installations are on the surveillance schedule.
Informal term for the briefing into a compartment. "Read in to" a compartment; "read out" on debriefing.
The instruction to report to an assigned facility immediately, overriding leave. Recall is issued by the duty officer on Council or facility commander authority.
The comparison of two records of the same quantity, with differences explained or carried forward. A reconciliation may be closed with differences carried forward.

The re-establishment of the functions of government from a relocation site following a catastrophic event. ALPHA-01 holds full government-in-exile capability; ALPHA-05 is the secondary reconstitution site.
The authorised destruction of controlled records by approved method, witnessed and certified. The Facility Inventory is destroyed immediately upon succession of Council membership.
The withholding of text from a reader below the required tier or without the required compartment. A redaction shows the withholding authority and reference, and nothing of the withheld content.
A sealed compartment with independent air supply, used as the muster point for fire and atmosphere emergencies below ground.
A facility to which an organisation moves its essential functions in an emergency. Used in cover documents in its ordinary federal sense.
Any storage device that can be detached from a workstation. Removable media are prohibited on MERIDIAN workstations except under a signed reproduction request.
The form required before any controlled document is copied, printed in more than one copy, or transferred to removable media. Documents marked for physical distribution only may not be reproduced.
The strategic stocks of food, water treatment, medical supply, energy and armaments held across the network, expressed at full 23,400-capacity scale unless otherwise noted.
The operation of a segment or link for scheduled movements of personnel and materiel. A segment may be complete and commissioned but NOT IN REVENUE SERVICE.
The numbered issue of a document. Revision authority for the Facility Inventory rests with a Council majority vote; for other documents, with the originator.
The vehicles of the rail and tram systems, registered by vehicle number, type and home depot.
The sheet attached to a document in circulation, listing offices in order of routing, the action officer, the suspense date and spaces for initials.
A DELTA-class surface or near-surface facility for emergency staging. Staffed by rotating guard only.
The current isolation condition of a facility or zone as displayed on telemetry: OPEN, CONDITIONED, SEALED, or SEALED (DRILL).
The agricultural seed collection at ALPHA-03, 1.2 million samples.
One of six numbered ALPHA-to-ALPHA rail tunnels, 01 to 06, each between two hubs.
The voluntary report by an individual of their own security violation. A timely self-report is considered in mitigation.
The automatic locking of a MERIDIAN workstation after a period without input. Session state is preserved; re-authentication is required.
The handover between watches, with signed transfer of the watch log. No possessions are granted or surrendered during shift change.
The civil time at a facility's surface location, shown in brackets after Zulu time.
The reduced complement maintaining a facility during low-manning periods, held at approximately 7:1 support-to-command to preserve institutional knowledge.
The cryptographic card inserted at the workstation to open a session. Removal of the token locks the session.
The assignment of office and berthing space within a facility, set by the facility administrative officer. Requests are reviewed quarterly.

Single Scope Background Investigation, conducted with the OSC supplement covering multi-generational family citizenship, financial independence from foreign-connected entities, psychological assessment for ideological reliability and social network mapping.
The Phase 5 objective (2013 to 2020): network staffing at 75 per cent of capacity, 17,550 personnel, with full redundancy across all facilities.
A firm engaged by a prime contractor. Subcontractors are not told the identity of the end user.
The replacement of a document by a later one, stated on the later document as "Supersedes".

The total number of berths across all 47 facilities: 34,700 (ALPHA 16,000, BETA 10,780, GAMMA 6,940, DELTA 980). Surge berthing is a physical count of berths and is not supported by reserves at full occupancy. Compare sustained capacity.
The date by which an action is due back to the tasking office. Written in the form 12 MAY 2008.

The number of personnel the network can support for the planned sustainment period at full reserves: 23,400. Used as the denominator of utilisation and as the scale at which reserves are stated. Compare surge berthing.
The period a facility can operate without resupply: ALPHA 12 to 18 months by site; GAMMA 90 to 180 days; DELTA 72 hours maximum; BETA limited.
A written instruction to a division or individual to take an action, with an action officer and a suspense date.
Tunnel boring machine. Rail and tram tunnels were driven by deep TBMs from 2002 to 2007 under classification as utility infrastructure and geological survey operations.
A printed card issued to a newly assigned individual bearing an operator ID and initial passphrase, valid until a permanent smart token is issued.

One of four personnel levels determining clearance and knowledge scope: Tier 1 Core Council (11); Tier 2 Facility Command Staff (247); Tier 3 Specialised Personnel (1,891); Tier 4 Essential Support (1,698). Total 3,847.
The working timetable of scheduled rail and tram movements, issued by Transit Control. Unscheduled movements are entered in the incident log.
The title of the United States Code governing war and national defence, under whose secrecy provisions all OSC contractors are bound.
The clearance held by Tier 3: Top Secret, Sensitive Compartmented Information, with access to one or more OSC compartments. Tier 4 holds TS/SCI with limited compartments.
The percentage of assigned training modules completed by their suspense dates, reported monthly by division.
The high-speed electric system linking ALPHA hubs to BETA facilities and BETA facilities to GAMMA facilities, operating at 90 mph average.
The form authorising official travel. Travel between facilities by rail or tram is authorised by Transit Control; surface travel by the division head.
The requirement that two authorised individuals be present for an action, each able to detect an incorrect act by the other.
The control system for OSC information. Markings are formed as UMBRA/OSC followed by a caveat.

Marking and clearance held by Tier 2: full awareness of the assigned facility and its immediate connections; limited awareness of the broader network. Written in source documents as UMBRA/OSC COMPARTMENTED.

Highest marking. Applied to Council documents, including the Facility Inventory, distributed in eleven numbered physical copies with no electronic copies permitted. Written in source documents as UMBRA/OSC EYES ONLY.
Marking applied to the Council Charter and to material restricted by Council instruction. Written in source documents as UMBRA/OSC RESTRICTED.
Clearance held by Tier 1, conferring full network awareness. Written in source documents as UMBRA/OSC UNRESTRICTED.
Current staffing as a percentage of sustained capacity (23,400): 3,847 persons, 16.4 per cent, as at May 2008.
The OSC supplement to the SSBI. See SSBI.
The bound register at each entry control point in which visitors, their escorts and times of entry and exit are recorded.
The office under whose authority a redaction is applied, shown with its reference when a redaction is examined. Only the withholding authority, or the Council, may release withheld text.
Coordinated Universal Time, written with the suffix Z. All MERIDIAN times are given in Zulu with site-local time in brackets.

docNumbering.notes: Four-digit serial, network-wide, never reused. Cited short-form as DIR-0412 in refusals and footers. Revisions keep the number and increment the revision; a replacement takes a new number and a supersession line.
YY = calendar year of issue. Serial resets each January. Issued by the originating division registry.
Formal site-to-site traffic over the key distribution network. Carries a date-time group (DTG) in the heading, e.g. 121430Z MAY 08.
One number per session. Six sessions a year in ordinary times.
Issued under the Secretary's signature.
Articles I-VII.

anomalies.title: The missing 790
anomalies.canonAnswer: Tier totals (3,847) count every person on the OSC payroll; facility staff (3,057) count only those posted to a site. The 790 difference is carried as "DETACHED / UNPOSTED", a payroll category no directive defines. It appears in personnel totals with no drill-down.

anomalies.title: 847 miles versus engineering length
anomalies.canonAnswer: 847 miles is the certified figure reported to the Council. Engineering tables give rail 6,074 miles (sum of six segments) and tram 10,538 miles (sum of four network totals, equal to the sum of the 27 listed links). The Transit app shows engineering figures; the Tier 1 summary shows 847. Neither is corrected.

anomalies.title: Sustained versus surge capacity
anomalies.canonAnswer: 23,400 is SUSTAINED CAPACITY: persons the network can keep alive at full reserves. 34,700 is SURGE BERTHING: the sum of every class's stated capacity. Utilization (16.4%) and phase targets use 23,400; facility pages use their own berthing figures.

anomalies.title: Segment 04 not in revenue service
anomalies.canonAnswer: Segment 04 (ALPHA-02 to ALPHA-05, 891 mi) appears in the segment table but in neither facility's connection list. It was completed March 2007 and is NOT IN REVENUE SERVICE. No reason is recorded.

anomalies.title: No electronic copies permitted
anomalies.canonAnswer: The Facility Inventory is distributed in 11 physical copies with no electronic copies permitted, yet a partially redacted scan of it is held in the Records Library. Records Division has an open security incident on it.

anomalies.title: Meal stocks imply one meal per person per day
anomalies.canonAnswer: 47 million meals for 23,400 persons for 5.5 years works out to 1.0 meal per person per day. At three meals a day the same stock lasts 670 days (1.83 years). The 5.5-year figure stands as the Council figure; the ration basis is not stated anywhere.

anomalies.title: Small-arms reserve arithmetic
anomalies.canonAnswer: "Full capacity + 400% reserve" means five weapons per armed position. 68,000 / 5 = 13,600, which matches neither 23,400 (117,000 needed) nor 34,700 (173,500). The figure stands; the basis for 13,600 is not given.

anomalies.title: Twelve primary hubs
anomalies.canonAnswer: The executive summary says the network connects 12 primary hub installations. Only the five ALPHA sites are called hubs anywhere in the source; twelve is the BETA count. Canon keeps 12 as the certified headline figure without a list behind it.

anomalies.title: Two utilization bases
anomalies.canonAnswer: The 16.4% headline divides tier totals (including the 790 unposted) by sustained capacity. Every facility and class percentage divides posted staff by that site's berthing (surge) figure. On one basis throughout, the network is 8.8% (posted / surge) or 13.1% (posted / sustained).

anomalies.title: Tram links shorter than the straight-line distance
anomalies.canonAnswer: Placed by their stated anchors, 17 of the 27 tram links are shorter than the great-circle distance between their end points (BETA-02 to GAMMA-03 is listed at 97 mi against about 201 mi). Rail segments are all longer than the straight line, as they should be. The listed mileages stand as engineering figures; the geographic view draws links between computed positions and does not label them with length.

anomalies.title: The 7:1 support-to-command ratio
anomalies.canonAnswer: Across the five ALPHA sites, 1,255 non-command staff to 162 command staff is 7.7:1 (sites range 5.8:1 to 9.8:1). Network-wide Tier 3 and 4 to Tier 1 and 2 is 13.9:1, and the full-staffing model (8% command) is 11.5:1. "Approximately 7:1" holds only for ALPHA command lines.

threatDetail.label: Nuclear Exchange
contingency: The network is designed for survival and for post-event governance. Facility depth and hardening are sufficient for a direct near-strike; rail and tram tunnels are EMP-rated and seismic-isolated.

On warning, ALPHA hubs assume SEALED state on Council or facility commander order. Transit Control suspends revenue service and holds consists at the nearest terminal. Essential personnel extraction to GAMMA-class shelters proceeds by the routes held at DELTA-class extraction route nodes.
Reconstitution is directed from ALPHA-01, with ALPHA-05 as the secondary reconstitution site. Facility sustainment windows and reserves are stated at sustained capacity, not surge berthing.

threatDetail.label: Biological / Chemical
contingency: All facilities are NBC-rated with 180-day seal capability. Seal state is held at CONDITIONED during normal operation, with air handling units on gas-phase filtration and positive pressure at the personnel doors.

On a biological or chemical indication, the affected facility goes to SEALED; adjacent facilities on the same network go to CONDITIONED pending assessment. BETA-03 holds the biomedical response function for the Southern Network.

threatDetail.label: Conventional Military
contingency: Facilities are hardened against direct strike, and depth is sufficient to survive surface detonation. The surface cover facility is not defended as such; its loss is planned for.
Security forces hold the shaft collars and portal approaches. Surface cover staff with no OSC access are evacuated under the cover agency's own procedures.

threatDetail.label: Outside Agency Discovery
contingency: Compartmentation prevents comprehensive understanding from a single-point compromise. No prime contractor knows more than three sites; no line item discloses the programme; no cover agency holds the network's existence.

An inquiry by an outside agency into a single site is answered by that site's cover identity, through the cover agency's ordinary channels. Inquiries that touch two or more sites are referred to the Office of Internal Assurance for assessment.

threatDetail.label: Congressional Investigation
contingency: Legal frameworks are established. Classification authorities prevent disclosure even under subpoena. Congressional oversight committees possess no awareness of programme existence.
Questions arising from appropriations review are answered at line-item level by the parent department, within the cover title of the line item concerned.

threatDetail.label: Whistleblowers
contingency: Personnel vetting and monitoring protocols minimise risk. The OSC supplement to the SSBI covers multi-generational family citizenship, financial independence from foreign-connected entities, psychological assessment for ideological reliability and social network mapping.

threatDetail.label: Media Exposure
contingency: Information warfare capabilities enable narrative control. Prepared cover stories exist for all facility types and are reviewed with each cover review.
A media inquiry concerning a site is answered by the cover agency's public affairs office using the published cover story. No OSC office responds to a media inquiry directly.

model.title: Hardened Site Survivability Estimator
model.disclaimer: Planning model PM-3 gives rounded, order-of-magnitude estimates for continuity planning only. It is not an engineering assessment and must not be cited as a statement of any facility's design rating. It takes no account of ground conditions, portal geometry, repeated events, fire, or loss of external services. Figures are notional.
method: Surface peak overpressure at a site is read from the contour table: range to a contour in statute miles = range coefficient x (yield in kt) to the power 1/3.

Between contours the overpressure is interpolated on logarithms of range and overpressure. Beyond the outermost contour the site is taken as unaffected. Inside the innermost contour the overpressure is above the range of the model.
Effective site rating = rated overpressure of the hardening class x (1 + depth coupling x model depth in thousands of feet).
Estimated condition is read from the ratio of site overpressure to effective rating. Inside the innermost contour the condition is NOT ASSURED.
Model depth is the facility depth of record. Where the depth of record is not held by the user, GAMMA sites are modelled at the planning depth below.

levels.title: First initiation
consequences: All remote hub circuits are dropped at the key distribution network switch. Rail and tram movements hold at the next station.
Network Operations, ALPHA-02, carries out line checks and restores the circuits without further action.
The initiation is entered in the workstation audit trail and reported to the Office of Internal Assurance. A written statement is required of the initiating operator.

levels.title: Second initiation
consequences: Circuits are held down for the full line-check period unless restored earlier by certificate.
The Deputy Commander, ALPHA-02, is notified as certifying officer for the hub. A Circuit Restoration Certificate may be raised at the panel and is routed to that officer.
The initiating operator is interviewed by the Resident Assurance Officer.

levels.title: Third initiation
consequences: Circuits remain down until a Circuit Restoration Certificate is approved by the Deputy Commander, ALPHA-02. There is no automatic restoration.
The Office of Internal Assurance records a formal finding against the initiating operator. The workstation is placed under review and the lock screen says so.
On restoration the cover of the control is fitted with a numbered tamper seal by the Resident Assurance Officer.

levels.title: Fourth initiation
consequences: The tamper seal must be broken before the cover can be lifted. The breaking of the seal is reported to the Office of Internal Assurance.
Circuits remain down until a Circuit Restoration Certificate is approved by the Deputy Commander, ALPHA-02.
An adverse report is entered on the probation record of the operator to whom the workstation is assigned, whoever initiated.

levels.title: Fifth initiation
consequences: The isolation is held. Restoration is reserved to the Council Secretariat and is not made from any workstation.
The control is withdrawn from service in the actuated position. No certificate is accepted at the panel.
The escalation level is not reduced by any procedure.

messages.title: Muster, all personnel
messages.text: Attention all personnel. Attention all personnel. Proceed now to your assigned muster point by the nearest stairway. Do not use the hoists or lifts. Take your badge. Report to the muster warden and remain at the muster point until released.

messages.title: Smoke reported, leave the zone
messages.text: Attention. Smoke has been reported in this zone. Leave the zone by the nearest marked exit and close doors behind you. Do not stop to collect belongings. Report to the muster warden at your assigned muster point.

messages.title: Air handling to filtered mode
messages.text: Attention all personnel. Air handling is changing over to filtered mode. Remain on your level. Keep doors closed. You may notice a change in pressure and in supply air noise. This is expected. Do not adjust room controls.

messages.title: Medical response team
messages.text: Medical response team. Medical response team. Report to the clinic for your location. Medical response team to the clinic.

messages.title: Air handling maintenance in this zone
messages.text: Attention please. Air handling maintenance is in progress in this zone. Supply air will be reduced for about forty minutes. Please leave doors as you find them and do not adjust room thermostats. Thank you.

messages.title: Domestic water interruption
messages.text: Attention please. Domestic water to this zone will be shut off shortly for planned work. Drinking water is available at the dining level. Please do not run taps while the supply is off. Thank you.

messages.title: Dining hall service times changed
messages.text: Attention please. Today's dining hall service times have changed. The revised times are posted at the servery and on the notice board at the lift lobby. Thank you.

messages.title: Personnel hoist out of service
messages.text: Attention please. The personnel hoist is out of service until further notice. Use the freight hoist by arrangement with the hoist operator, or the stairways. Do not use the egress winder except in an emergency.

messages.title: Badge found, security desk
messages.text: Attention please. A personnel badge has been handed in at the security desk. If you have mislaid your badge, collect it from the desk in person. Thank you.

messages.title: Standby generator run on load
messages.text: Attention please. The standby generator will be run on load for its scheduled test. Lighting may dip briefly at changeover and again at the end of the test. Equipment on protected supplies is not affected.

messages.title: Seal drill, doors closing
messages.text: Seal drill. Seal drill. This is a drill. Portal and blast doors are closing. Clear all doorways. Go to your muster point and report to the muster warden. This is a drill.

messages.title: Seal drill, site sealed
messages.text: This is a drill. The site is sealed. Remain at your muster point. Wardens, report your count. This is a drill.

messages.title: Seal drill, stand down
messages.text: The seal drill is ended. Stand down. Return to your normal duties. Doors will be restored to normal positions by the door controller.

messages.title: Seal drill, cancelled
messages.text: The seal drill is cancelled. Stand down. Return to your normal duties. Do not open doors that remain closed; the door controller will restore them.

messages.title: Inter-site communications interrupted
messages.text: Attention all personnel. Communications with other sites are interrupted. Remain at your post. Messages for other sites will be held until communications are restored. Do not call the switchboard to report the interruption.

messages.title: Inter-site communications restored
messages.text: Attention please. Communications with other sites are restored. Held messages will be delivered in order of precedence.

messages.title: Weekly tone test
messages.text: This is a test of the public address system. No action is required. This is a test.
